v0.1.6b.notes:
AgentRT v0.1.6b (patch)

v0.1.6a could not start on many systems: the daemon fleet failed to come
up ("many libraries not found", all daemons/gateway/heapstore offline),
the hero banner corrupted its bottom border in narrow terminals, and
binaries required GLIBC >= 2.38 so older distros refused to run them.

Root causes (all fixed in 0.1.6b):

- DT_RUNPATH is not transitive: a daemon's direct deps were found via
  $ORIGIN/../lib, but the transitive deps of those libs (libcurl ->
  libgnutls/librtmp/libssh/libldap, ...) were resolved only through the
  host system paths. On hosts missing those libs, every daemon died at
  startup. Fix: the launcher/bootstrap now sources agentrt-env.sh which
  injects LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<install>/lib (transitive for all children);
  the runtime libs are self-contained inside the package lib/.
- Binaries were built on a glibc 2.39 host, so every artifact demanded
  GLIBC >= 2.38 ("one user could start it, several could not"). Fix:
  all three architectures are now built inside ubuntu:20.04 containers
  (glibc 2.31 baseline) and the .so closure is collected inside the
  container against that baseline, so the package runs on Ubuntu 20.04
  and newer.
- Hero banner: the frame width had a hard 74-column minimum, so on
  terminals narrower than ~78 cols the frame wrapped, grew past the
  pinned 7 lines, and the dialogue overwrote the bottom border (missing
  bottom line + overlapping garbled text). Fix: the frame now adapts to
  the terminal width (UTF-8-safe clipping keeps the box intact).
- Build chain fixes: single OpenSSL authority inside the build container
  (self-built 3.0.17, libdir normalized to lib/ so find_package resolves
  one version — the system 1.1.1f on Ubuntu 20.04 does not export
  EVP_DigestSignUpdate), apt toolchain reinstalled on every container
  instance (previous flag-file skip left new instances without gcc), and
  the Rust TUI linker is chosen on demand (ld.lld only when present).

Upgrade: run `airymaxrt update` (0.1.6a users) or reinstall with the
one-line installer to get the fixed launcher + self-contained libs.
